messages:
alex: heads-up: started seeing 95th/99th tail spikes on prod-scheduler after the 02:30 deploy. 95p jumped from ~60ms to ~220ms. throughput down ~12%. graphs: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abc/scheduler
lee: yikes. which deploy? any config changes in the scheduler?
anita: alex which model/route is hottest? KV cache miss rate changed?
alex: deploy id `deploy-2026-03-17-02` (kernel-selector v2). affected mainly short-seq routes: chat-fast and convo-preview. KV miss ratio up ~3x on those routes.
jason: can you paste the scheduler logs for a few minutes around the spike?
alex: paste logs (truncated):
```
[02:29:58] admit: token_bucket=0.4 target_batch=16 actual_batch=6
[02:30:01] kernel_select: selected kernel=matmul_fused_v2 (was matmul_fused_v1)
[02:30:01] kvcache: miss_rate=0.21 (prev=0.07)
[02:30:02] schedule: microbatch_timeout=4ms -> forced flush
[02:30:03] latency P95=215ms P99=412ms
```
lee: interesting — kernel switch aligns with KV miss and smaller microbatches. matmul_fused_v2 has a faster steady-state but worse cold-start locality?
profiler-bot: profiler snapshot uploaded: s3://profiler/prod/scheduler/1794005678/trace-1.pb
anita: ran a quick trace locally: matmul_fused_v2 path falls back to a different memory layout which increases KV lookup jitter. also observed more memcpy calls in kernel prologue.
jason: could this be noisy neighbor or GPU-level scheduling? any host-level pressure?
alex: no obvious GPU contention on the nodes in the affected pool. node-level GPU util steady. but one host had another high-throughput job at 02:28 — not co-located with the highest latency pool though.
lee: hypothesis: kernel selector change causes slightly different per-request time distribution -> admission token bucket sees more short fast completions and then frequent small microbatches -> microbatching timeout triggers more often -> increases tail due to more frequent flushes and higher KV miss overhead.
anita: +1. Also kernel's mem layout increases KV lookup latency variance, which is expensive for short sequences where KV access is a bigger fraction.
sre-oncall: tagging this as P2 perf regression. initiating rollback window and paging infra. @infra-bot can you start a canary rollback? :rotating_light:
infra-bot: rollback job queued -> canary rollback to kernel-selector v1 on 3 nodes in pool chat-fast. ETA 8m.
jason: meanwhile can we mitigate via admission knobs? try bumping microbatch_timeout from 4ms to 8ms for short routes and increase min_batch_size to 8 to avoid tiny microbatches.
lee: good call. I'll push a config change to canary routes (chat-fast, convo-preview) to microbatch_timeout=8ms and min_batch=8, non-blocking.
alex: also adding a KV-cache warmup: extend prefetch window for short routes to reduce miss cold starts.
anita: i'll open a small PR to revert kernel selector change (PR #345) if rollback isn't clean.
sre-oncall: update: canary rollback completed on 3 nodes. early metrics look better (95p down to ~70ms on canary).
jason: after the admission tweak on canary, saw P95 drop to 85ms. seems both rollback and admission fixes help.
lee: plan: 1) revert kernel-selector change in next deploy (PR created), 2) make microbatch_timeout adaptive (experiment), 3) add telemetry to kernel selector to capture KV-miss correlation, 4) add a regression test in perf-suite that simulates short-seq KV-heavy workloads.
anita: also add a perf assertion: any kernel selector change must ship with per-arch KV-latency microbench.
alex: agreed. creating follow-ups: ACTIONS: alex -> perf-suite test, lee -> adaptive admission spike, anita -> PR and bench, jason -> run node-level noisy-neighbor sim in staging.
profiler-bot: perf trace diff attached: s3://profiler/prod/diffs/1794005678/diff.html
sre-oncall: marking incident resolved for now, leaving monitoring alert open for 24h. if 95p > 120ms re-open. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks all — good catch. lessons: kernel selection changes can affect memory layout & KV behavior; admission heuristics need to be robust to selector-induced variance.
jason: will add a short postmortem note in #incidents after metrics settle.
lee: FYI i've flagged PR templates to require KV perf benchmark results when touching kernel selection logic. :thumbsup:
anita: one more: add a small e2e microbench that runs synthetic KV-heavy short sequences at scale before deploys.
alex: ack. closing thread once postmortem is up.
